findingCounts.note: Counts of identified findings, not a guarantee of absent undiscovered defects.

findings.title: OCI snapshots ignore tenant/user/namespace identity
findings.preconditions: Shared host workspace/stateDirectory and equal runId across different scopes; caller can supply runId. No compromised daemon, raw state-file access or provider is needed.
findings.observed: runHarness for tenant B completed and returned tenant A private unimported candidate through read_file.
findings.impact: Confidentiality and integrity isolation between scoped runs is not enforced for OCI artifacts. Import/cancellation collateral effects require additional tests; no host escape claimed.
findings.recommendation: Bind artifact directory, metadata, patch identity, runtime resources and cleanup to canonical workspace + full scope + run identity. Reject or explicitly migrate legacy unscoped artifacts; test cross-scope resume/import/cleanup.
findings.acceptance: Different scopes with identical runId cannot inspect, modify, import or clean each other artifacts; same-scope resume remains functional.

findings.title: Concurrent approved writes both pass the same digest precondition
findings.preconditions: Two writers publish different approved changes to the same existing file from the same baseline.
findings.observed: Both writes succeeded with a deterministic checkpoint barrier; an earlier non-instrumented 20-trial probe accepted both in 18 trials. Sequential stale writes were rejected.
findings.impact: Lost update and inaccurate assumption that both approved baseline transitions were valid; no approval bypass or filesystem escape demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Serialize host mutation transactions across runs/processes with bounded crash-safe ownership and recheck preconditions inside publication protection. Keep rollback ownership-aware.
findings.acceptance: Exactly one conflicting update succeeds; other fails stale/conflict, including concurrent OCI imports and rollback.

findings.title: Replacement approval hides replacement text in its default card
findings.preconditions: apply_reviewed_replacement oldText exceeds the default summary length.
findings.observed: newText fixture marker absent from summary. Omission notice and explicit full view are present.
findings.impact: A built-in mutation can be approved without its replacement text being shown by default. This is review visibility failure, not silent execution.
findings.recommendation: Include replacement in exact-review tools and cover all authority-bearing mutation tools in rendering tests.
findings.acceptance: Default built-in replacement card shows full approved oldText/newText and digest, with terminal controls escaped.

findings.title: Formal authority inventory omits read_task and repair_plan
findings.observed: Inventory lacks both tools; its existing parity test constructs the catalog without createTaskTools, so it passes.
findings.impact: Review coverage gate cannot detect these new model-facing capabilities; no runtime privilege escalation demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Derive/check complete catalog including task tools, update coverage and reviewer dossier.
findings.acceptance: Inventory comparison against the actual full tool set passes and fails if any class is removed.

controls.assessment: Descriptor-bound reads, strict relative edit paths, digest-bound proposals and bounded context/skill loading inspected. Task source inventory needs correction.
controls.residualRisk: Trusted project instructions may influence model behavior within granted tool authority.

controls.assessment: Mutating tools retain interrupt approvals; reserved MCP names cannot replace local tools. Model-authored repair state schedules tools through approval. Replacement card has a visibility defect.
controls.residualRisk: Provider receives prompts and may return adversarial content; operators must scope data and review approvals.

controls.assessment: HTTP URL/header policy, redirect rejection, bounded bodies, RPC IDs and permission-derived approvals inspected. Injection regex is a heuristic, not a security boundary.
controls.residualRisk: An approved remote MCP service can observe the inputs explicitly sent to it.

controls.assessment: Canonical input digest, tool/environment version, approval identity, optional signer and journal claim inspected. File publication is not atomic with its precondition; replacement review is truncated.
controls.residualRisk: Paused approvals require the original artifact and cannot be rebound across incompatible policy versions.

controls.assessment: Run/session queries bind scope, but OCI artifact identity omits it. Cross-scope candidate disclosure reproduced through runHarness.
controls.residualRisk: A process with direct filesystem access to the local state directory remains inside the trust boundary.

controls.assessment: Strict provider/model schema, owner-only file permissions, single-link and no-follow reads inspected. Profile data cannot set tools or execution permissions.
controls.residualRisk: A compromised operator account or host filesystem can still replace the selected provider/model configuration.

controls.assessment: OCI uses network none, read-only root, dropped capabilities, resource bounds, no inherited environment and separate import. Snapshot scope collision remains open.
controls.residualRisk: Containers are not VMs; the host kernel and OCI daemon are trusted.

controls.assessment: SQLite WAL, scoped leases/revisions and backup transaction checks inspected. Per-run ownership does not serialize distinct runs publishing into the same host file.
controls.residualRisk: Power loss and external filesystem corruption still require operator backup and recovery.

controls.assessment: Pinned actions, immutable transfer checks and source/workflow/digest provenance checks inspected. Final RC14 protected release and current advisory audit remain unavailable.
controls.residualRisk: Registry, GitHub, npm, and maintainer identities remain external trust dependencies.

controls.assessment: Explicit trust assumption retained. This review does not establish VM isolation or protection from the host/daemon operator.
controls.residualRisk: The harness cannot protect against an already compromised host, kernel, container daemon, or maintainer account.

trustBoundaries.assessment: Reviewed terminal rendering, durable approvals and input/environment binding. Full replacement payload is not shown by default.
Providers cannot authorize local mutations. Prompt disclosure to configured providers and heuristic redaction remain operator risks.
Repository/attachment text is bounded and untrusted. No-follow reads and path restrictions were inspected; prompt injection cannot be eliminated by filtering.
HTTPS/loopback policy and explicit credential headers; redirects rejected. Configured service identity and custom client remain trusted integration choices.
Host checks remain trusted host execution; OCI commands use explicit argv/shell approval. An allowed interpreter can run arbitrary code within that authority.
Reviewed daemon policy, snapshot validation and import. Artifact scope isolation fails when run IDs coincide.
Private SQLite files, scoped stores and durable ownership inspected. OCI filesystem artifacts bypass scoped identity; host file updates race.
Strict schema, explicit selection, safe file read and private permissions. A compromised operator account remains trusted.
Least-privilege workflow declarations, pinned actions, protected publish/live environments and no persisted checkout credentials inspected. Repository settings not re-audited.
Digest/source/workflow provenance checks inspected. Registry trust and final published RC14 provenance are not replaced by the local tarball.
Exact local tarball installed in prior same-session validation. Final signed/published artifact remains unverified and dependency advisories returned 503.
